Katie — thanks for the clear ask. Below are two pragmatic structures that customers commonly use to preserve rate certainty while keeping ramp flexibility. I’m attaching a short, worked example and a draft SOW you can share with Finance.

Option A — 24-month staged prepay (Preferred)
- Term: 24 months; locks current effective token/embedding rates for the term.
- Payment cadence: 40% deposit at signing, 30% at month 6, 30% at month 12 (applied as prepaid credits).
- Usage true-up: annual reconciliation; unused credits roll forward within term but not beyond term end; unused balance refundable pro-rata in year 2 if reduced usage triggers lower committed tier (subject to 90-day notice).
- Discount: 15% off list per-token rate (vs current hosted list) if the deposit schedule is accepted.

Option B — 36-month annualized prepay (Conservative)
- Term: 36 months; locks price for whole term.
- Payment cadence: annual prepay installments (pay-as-you-go annually in advance).
- Usage true-up: annual true-up with 12-month carry-forward; partial refunds allowed at year 3 close if actuals materially lower (>25% variance).
- Discount: 20% off list per-token rate.

Key behavioral protections we recommend
- Ramp credits: we can include a staged credit allocation that matches your projected ramp (you provide forecast for months 1–12).
- Burndown reporting: monthly usage + remaining credit dashboard access in Redwood Console.
- Failover: automatic fallback to a compatible lower-cost model if capacity constraints occur (no impact to price lock).

Next steps
1) Choose A or B (or request a hybrid)
2) We’ll produce a numeric schedule with projected credits and a short SOW (1–2 pages) for Finance review
3) Sign & exchange the initial deposit; DocuSign link provided when ready

I’ve attached the worked example that maps your current FY usage to the two options so you can compare total cost and cash flow. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Best,
